about.body: This is a second page, translated like the first.
fallback.only_en: This sentence is missing from the Ukrainian catalog.
demo.intro: Every string on this page comes from a translation catalog. Switch the language and watch each feature react.
demo.switcher.title: Switch the language
demo.switcher.body: One call re-renders every translated element, and the choice is remembered for your next visit.
demo.interpolation.title: Parameters
demo.interpolation.body: A value drops in where the translator put the placeholder, so the word order stays the translator's call.
demo.interpolation.label: Your name
demo.plural.title: Plurals that know the language
demo.plural.body: ICU plural rules: English has one and other, Ukrainian one, few and many. Change the count and compare.
demo.tags.title: Markup inside a translation
demo.tags.body: The catalog wraps the words in a link tag. The translator chooses where the link sits in the sentence; your app decides what it points to and how it renders.
demo.formatting.title: Dates and numbers
demo.formatting.body: Intl formats follow the locale: thousands separators, month names and the date order.
demo.lazy.title: Load translations on demand
demo.lazy.body: The selected language and its English fallback load first. Another language loads when you select it, and the account namespace when its page opens.
demo.lazy.namespaces: Namespaces active for every fetched locale: {namespaces}
demo.fallback.title: Fallbacks and missing keys
demo.fallback.body: A key missing in Ukrainian falls back to English. A key missing everywhere shows its name, so you notice it in development.
demo.missing.title: A missing parameter stays visible
demo.missing.body: The placeholder remains in the text instead of disappearing silently.
demo.navigation.title: A second page, the same locale
demo.navigation.body: The locale survives navigation, and the account namespace loads on demand.
demo.select.title: Select by a value
demo.select.body: ICU select picks a whole sentence by a value, here the reviewer's gender. In English only the pronoun changes; switch to Ukrainian and the verb ending changes too. The app passes one value, the translator writes each variant.
demo.select.message: {gender, select, female {She replied to your review} male {He replied to your review} other {They replied to your review}}
demo.ordinal.title: Ordinals
demo.ordinal.body: selectordinal knows that English says 1st, 2nd, 3rd and Ukrainian does not. The number is the counter above, rendered as an ordinal.
demo.ordinal.message: You are the {n, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} visitor today.
demo.rtl.body: Arabic turns the whole page right-to-left: <html dir> follows the locale.
demo.options.title: Call options
demo.options.body: One call can read another locale or namespace. The names below render each language in its own language; switch languages to grow the list.
demo.options.name: English
demo.typed.title: Typed keys
demo.typed.body: The keys are generated from these JSON files: a misspelled key or a missing parameter is a compile error. Open src/i18n in the editor and try it.
demo.errors.title: Every failure reaches a hook
demo.errors.body: t() never throws. A key that no catalog has is reported to onError as missing_key, wired here to a counter you could send to your tracker. A catalog that fails to load is reported there as load_failed, which this page does not show.
demo.formality.title: Formal or informal
demo.formality.body: English has one way to address someone; German has Sie and du, Ukrainian Ви and ти. One select value lets each translator pick the register, and the English stays a single sentence.
demo.formality.message: {formality, select, formal {Welcome back. Your seat is saved.} other {Welcome back. Your seat is saved.}}
demo.start.intro: One package, one translated line, one switcher. This is the whole integration.
